newsitem.title: BANGLADESH: Bangladeshi port to pay fine for handling delay.
newsitem.headline: Bangladeshi port to pay fine for handling delay.

text.p: The Singapore-based Chittagong Feeder Trade Committee (CFTC) imposed a temporary congestion surcharge on Bangladesh's main Chittagong port due to delays in handling shipments, port officials said on Monday.

The officials said the CFTC informed the port authority about the surcharge on Saturday. It would be effective immediately and last for one month. The daily surcharge rate was $150 for a 20-foot container and $300 for 40-foot container, they said.
The U.S.-based Asia North America Eastbound Rate Agreement (ANERA) has also announced the imposition of surcharge of $250 for a 20-foot container from August 25, they said.
The CFTC said it would withdraw the surcharge if the port authority could clear the congestion within a month, the officials said.

"We have taken a lot of measures including ensuring round-the-clock handling of cargo, especially containers from early August when the CFTC issued the warning," said Captain Zahiruddin Mahmood, a Chittagong Port operations official and chief of the task force constituted to speed up handling.
The port handled about 20,000 tonnes cargo per day in the past week compared with a daily average of 13,000 tonnes in July.
At the moment about 1,500 containers are handled per day against 1,000 in July. The handling rate was increasing gradually, a traffic officer at the port said.
There were 25 ships berthed at the port and 23 others at outer anchorages on Monday.
Lubricant oil importer Mohammad Ali said the surcharge would push up the price of imported commodities in the Bangladesh market.
"The poor consumers will he hard hit by the move," he said.
